verdict.rationale: Yubico's first-party SSH guide explains how to generate SSH keys directly on the FIDO2 YubiKey with OpenSSH. The private key never leaves the hardware, and a touch (user presence) is required for cryptographic operations. PIV and OpenPGP are documented as on-device private-key signing via PKCS#11 and smartcard interfaces, and community reports corroborate ed25519 FIDO SSH keys and touch-to-sign. Missing for 10: explicit documentation of SSH usage and touch policy for the PIV and OpenPGP paths specifically.

support.subject: As a developer, my SSH keys can be hardware-backed on the device — via FIDO2 sk-ssh keys, PIV, or OpenPGP — so server access requires a physical touch

citations.quote: This guide shows how to generate and use SSH keys directly on your FIDO2 security key with OpenSSH.
FIDO2 also requires user presence (a touch on your YubiKey) for cryptographic operations
you can generate the private key directly on the hardware, where it cannot be exported or extracted
It enables RSA or ECC sign/encrypt operations using a private key stored on a smartcard (such as the YubiKey), through common interfaces like PKCS#11.
It enables RSA or ECC sign/encrypt operations using a private key stored on a smartcard (such as YubiKeys)
